analysis.summary_en: We evaluated whether detection of A(H1N1) and A(H3N2) during the same admission identifies a high-risk phenotype in adults hospitalized with influenza-associated community-acquired pneumonia. This retrospective single-center study linked clinical and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid pathogen-spectrum records. Influenza A was detected by RT-PCR and BALF pathogens by targeted next-generation sequencing. Among 97 adults (51 H1N1 mono-positive; 46 dual-positive), dual positivity was associated with lower PaO2/FiO2 (244.17 vs 293.94; p=0.018), higher CRP and IL-6, more invasive ventilation (23.9% vs 7.8%; p=0.047), and more fungal co-detection (47.8% vs 25.5%; p=0.034). In-hospital death was 15.2% versus 3.9% (p=0.081). Dual positivity identified a severe hypoxemic phenotype with greater fungal co-detection. Oxygenation was the principal clinical correlate of excess risk.

title: The Resurgence of Respiratory Viruses After COVID-19: Molecular Insights from Pediatric SARI in Kashmir.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory viruses are major causes of severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) in children, yet molecular epidemiology data from northern India, particularly after the COVID-19 pandemic, remains sparse. This study addressed the knowledge gap by determining the prevalence and distribution of respiratory viral pathogens among hospitalized pediatric SARI patients in Kashmir.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective study was conducted from October 2023 to April 2025 at Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences, Srinagar. Children aged ≤15 years meeting the World Health Organization SARI case definition were enrolled, resulting in a total of 326 pediatric SARI cases.
analysis.methods: Nasopharyngeal and/or oropharyngeal samples were collected and tested using real-time polymerase chain reaction assays for SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and B, Respiratory Syncytial virus (RSV) A and B, Adenovirus, Human metapneumovirus, Rhinovirus, and Para-influenza viruses.
analysis.main_results: At least one respiratory virus was detected in 200 patients (61.3%). RSV was the most frequently detected virus, with RSV-B identified in 111 cases (34.0%) and RSV-A in 26 cases (7.9%). Influenza viruses accounted for a smaller proportion, including influenza A(H1N1) in 12 cases (3.6%), influenza A(H3N2) in 6 cases (1.8%), and influenza B (Victoria lineage) in 21 cases (6.4%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that respiratory viruses account for a substantial proportion of pediatric SARI cases in Kashmir, with RSV emerging as the predominant pathogen in the post-pandemic period. This study provides novel molecular insights into the resurgence of respiratory viruses in a previously understudied region.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Strengthening molecular surveillance may improve diagnostic stewardship and guide targeted prevention strategies for pediatric SARI in northern India.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single-centre design and lack of longitudinal follow-up, which may affect generalisability and temporal trends assessment. The evidence is moderate, as it relies on a prospective design but lacks randomization and broader geographic representation.

analysis.summary_en: This prospective study from October 2023 to April 2025 at Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences, Srinagar, investigated respiratory viral pathogens in 326 hospitalized pediatric SARI cases aged ≤15 years. Using RT-PCR assays, at least one virus was detected in 61.3% of patients, with RSV-B (34.0%) and RSV-A (7.9%) being the most prevalent. Influenza viruses were less common, including A(H1N1) (3.6%), A(H3N2) (1.8%), and B (Victoria lineage) (6.4%). Most infections occurred in winter and predominantly affected infants. The authors conclude that respiratory viruses, particularly RSV, account for a substantial burden of pediatric SARI in Kashmir post-pandemic, highlighting the need for enhanced molecular surveillance and targeted prevention strategies.

title: Influenza vaccine awareness and uptake patterns among women of reproductive age in Pudong New Area: A community-based cross-sectional study

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the low uptake of influenza vaccination among pregnant women in China, a priority group for vaccination according to the World Health Organization, despite the absence of targeted policies and limited public health promotion in this context.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A community-based cross-sectional survey was conducted among women of reproductive age (15–49 years) in Pudong New Area, Shanghai, to assess influenza and vaccine awareness, vaccination route preferences, and influencing factors.
analysis.methods: The survey evaluated knowledge and attitudes via standardized questionnaires, analyzed using chi-square tests and multivariate logistic regression to identify predictors of vaccine knowledge and uptake.
analysis.main_results: The knowledge score among women of reproductive age was 3.77 ± 1.23, with a pass rate of 60.61%, while the influenza vaccine knowledge score was 3.55 ± 1.66 with a pass rate of 56.46%. Education level and being a healthcare professional were significant predictors of higher vaccine knowledge pass rates.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors highlight that healthcare workers had the highest cognitive levels regarding influenza vaccination, and that preferences for vaccination routes shift markedly in hypothetical pregnancy scenarios, with a notable decline in injection preference and increase in nasal spray preference.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that strengthening guidance from obstetricians, promoting non-injectable influenza vaccines, and delivering targeted health education could improve vaccination uptake among women of reproductive age in this setting.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which precludes causal inference, and the reliance on self-reported data, which may introduce bias. The evidence strength is assessed as moderate due to these constraints.

analysis.summary_en: This community-based cross-sectional study in Shanghai’s Pudong New Area examined influenza vaccine awareness and uptake patterns among women of reproductive age (15–49 years). The survey revealed moderate knowledge levels about influenza and vaccines, with pass rates of 60.61% and 56.46%, respectively. Healthcare professionals demonstrated higher cognitive levels, and education was a key predictor of vaccine knowledge. Notably, preferences for vaccination routes shifted significantly in hypothetical pregnancy scenarios, with a sharp decline in injection preference (from 41.25% to 13.31%) and an increase in nasal spray preference (from 10.60% to 23.17%). The authors propose that targeted interventions, such as strengthening obstetrician guidance, promoting non-injectable vaccines, and enhancing health education, could improve vaccination uptake in this population.
